events.title: Claudius Confirmed as Roman Emperor
events.description: A day after Caligula was assassinated, the Roman Senate confirmed Claudius as emperor. Claudius had been found by the Praetorian Guard, and he was an unlikely successor.
events.significance: Claudius went on to rule for 13 years. He expanded the empire, most notably with the conquest of Britain.

events.title: Henry VIII Marries Anne Boleyn
events.description: Henry VIII of England secretly married Anne Boleyn. He did so while his earlier marriage to Catherine of Aragon was still officially unresolved.
events.significance: The marriage accelerated England's break with the Catholic Church. It also led to the birth of the future Elizabeth I.

events.title: The League of Nations Is Founded
events.description: At the Paris Peace Conference, delegates agreed to create the League of Nations. It was an international body meant to settle disputes and prevent another world war.
events.significance: The League ultimately failed to prevent World War II. It nonetheless served as the model for the United Nations.

events.title: First Winter Olympics Open in Chamonix
events.description: The first Winter Olympic Games opened in Chamonix, in the French Alps. Athletes competed in events such as skiing, skating, ice hockey and bobsleigh.
events.significance: The event established a winter counterpart to the Summer Games. It grew into a major global sporting event.

events.title: Opportunity Rover Lands on Mars
events.description: NASA's Opportunity rover touched down on Mars, three weeks after its twin, Spirit. The mission was planned to last about 90 days.
events.significance: Opportunity kept operating for nearly 15 years. It found strong evidence that ancient Mars had liquid water.
